## What

Do not assume that a committed-source notice in the launcher means a Vitest worker also executed HEAD. Inspect the execution boundary. The loader's notice identifies its PID and entrypoint, and explains that a child without that loader can read working-tree bytes. A shell-fixture test can also read its subject with readFileSync and execute the extracted shell function directly.

This is a narrow local-verification route. It does not qualify a committed release, a frozen native host, or an unrelated imported module.

## Why it matters

In EI-28893377451755789, the agent unnecessarily waited for git-sync before testing a changed shell admission message and its fixture. The maintained test:file runner subsequently executed the new early-admission cases from the dirty test file. A launcher-only notice for coord-lifecycle/records.ts was not a substitution of the shell subject or the test worker.

## How to apply

1. Run the maintained project test command. Keep the loader, provenance checks and ledger reporter enabled.
2. Require execution of the changed cases, including a positive control. A pass from an older collection is not evidence.
3. Capture SHA256 of both the fixture and the shell subject before and after the run. The runner's named-path stamp covers only the paths it names; account separately for the directly read shell subject.
4. Read the final TEST_FILE_RESULT, process-specific substitution notices and canonical ledger row. Record local/dirty provenance explicitly. Do not generalize childSubstituted=0 into a claim about every launcher process or the entire import graph.
5. Keep any committed-source/native-host requirement on the separate acceptance step that actually needs it.

The maintained command was npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/verify-tauri-copy-bootstrap.test.ts --reporter=verbose.
